title: align-backpressure-to-sse-fragment-boundary-and-utf8-rescue
author: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: Under heavy concurrent streaming load the SSE reassembly window could be prematurely backpressured at the wrong byte offset, which in practice produced truncated UTF-8 runes, mis-ordered tool/function-call sentinels, and unrecoverable partial JSON payloads in the OpenAI-compat layer. This manifested as two visible classes of errors: 1) cheap client connections that were hit by backpressure would see mid-codepoint truncation and a "malformed UTF-8" parse path; 2) multi-segment events with function_call markers could have event boundaries shifted across the backpressure cut, producing interleaved tokens and duplicated sentinel sequences. Motivation: stabilize streaming output for customers using structured responses and function/tool calling (especially in platforms bridging OpenAI-compatible clients). Goal: ensure backpressure aligns to fragment/event boundaries when possible, transparently rescue incomplete UTF-8 runes and partial JSON fragments, and preserve strict ordering for function-call sentinels so downstream parsers never receive duplicated or reordered function tokens. Summary of changes: - Introduced a boundary-aware backpressure window in the sse/streamer layer that prefers draining up to the next event terminator (

 or data: ) when under pressure, falling back after a short timeout. - Added a UTF-8 rune reassembly helper: keep up to 4 trailing bytes in the fragment buffer and attempt a low-cost validation/rescue pass before emitting; if rescue fails, emit an explicit resync marker ("event: __resync__

") so clients can fast-fail or retry. - Implemented a function-call sentinel latch in the openai_compat module: an emitted function_call start token is never split across a forced backpressure cut; if the event is large, we escalate to an internal short-lived buffer and schedule a high-priority flush. - Added sequence-anchor metadata to SSE spans so the stream-stitcher can enforce relative ordering for concurrent shards and avoid duplicate sentinel replays during reassembly. - Extended the sse parser tests with fuzzed partial-byte splits and integrated a deterministic replay harness used in the failing incident noted in SUP-1287. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag `sse_boundary_backpressure=true` and default-on for Hosted API; dedicated customers can toggle via runtime config. The change is backwards-compatible at the protocol level: when the feature is off, behavior is unchanged. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for boundary alignment and rune rescue - [x] integration test with function_call sentinel stress - [x] CI flake triage and rerun pass - [x] added logging gated behind debug flag for post-deploy diagnostics - [x] Linear tickets linked for followups Impact and risk: The change touches the hot path in the serving runtime and was optimized to add a bounded memory window and a short timeout to avoid long-held buffers. We observed <0.7% p50 latency regression in the worst-case synthetic throughput test but eliminated a ~3% error tail caused by malformed frames. Follow-ups: - ENG-4302: add opt-out telemetry for customers that need raw byte-level stream semantics - ENG-4339: consider a client hint header to prefer strict emit vs boundary-rescue

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Can we make the rescue heuristic opt-in via a runtime flag? I want Dedicated customers to be able to opt-out. — ACK, made it a flag and default-on for Hosted.

Lina Chen: The UTF-8 rescue could mask real data corruption. Please add a resync marker so clients can detect when we did best-effort repair. — Added explicit event: __resync__ marker when rescue fails.

Marcus O'Neill: Stress test results look good but observe the p50 regression. Do we have telemetry to measure customer impact? — Added sse_boundary_rescues_total and a toggleable debug log; will follow up with ENG-4302 for telemetry opt-outs.
